v1.1.2 — a node that fell behind catches up from several peers at once

No reset, no coordinated update: replace the binary and restart; data, key and stake stay. This
release changes nothing a block contains or how it is executed. Protocol 2 activates at block
750000 as voted; 1.1.0, 1.1.1 and 1.1.2 all run it. **A node still on 1.0.x stops at block
750000** and goes on as soon as it runs 1.1.0 or later.

**Why update: a validator that misses a block can fall further and further behind**

On 2026-10-21 the production validator missed one block and then could not get back to the tip
for half an hour, 340 blocks behind at worst. It caught up again on its own, but from protocol 2
on a validator that stays behind long enough is jailed, and a jail costs stake.

The cause was how a node fetches the blocks it missed: one request at a time. Under load each
answer took 10 to 30 seconds whatever its size — five blocks or twenty-seven, the same — while the
chain added a block every 2.2 seconds. At about five blocks per twenty seconds the node lost ground
with every answer, and each answer that timed out halved the next request on top.

- **A node that is behind now asks up to four peers at once**, each for its own range of blocks,
  and applies the answers in order. A peer that answers slowly no longer holds up the others.
  Nothing is fetched twice: catching up costs the network the same bytes as before, spread over
  more uplinks.
- **A batch is no longer thrown away because the node's own tip moved while it was on its way.**
  A batch that reaches back below the tip is shortened and applied, and the peer that served it is
  no longer treated as if it had served something wrong — on 2026-10-21 that happened three times
  in six minutes, each time costing a whole request and sending the node away from an honest peer.

Measured on the production validator after deploying it: in the sixty blocks after the restart it
co-signed 58, the two it missed being the restart itself.
